class_id: a check whose premise is true in only ONE lifecycle state, applied to all of them
feature: scripts/lib/substance-checks.mjs (checkDegenerateBookbuildingBand); any predicate encoding a domain rule that holds during part of an entity's life
symptom: checkDegenerateBookbuildingBand encoded 'a book-built issue ALWAYS has floor < cap (SEBI ICDR)'. True while the book is OPEN; false afterwards, because after price discovery a book-built issue HAS one price and every source publishes it that way. Measured at the source (Chittorgarh report 82, FY2026-27): all 183 CLOSED book-built rows carry a single price, only the 18 STILL-OPEN ones carry a range. On staging the check fired on 239 real IPOs and exempted none, of which the large majority were correct data. THE COST IS NOT THE NOISE, IT IS THE SIGNAL BURIED: 21 genuine defects sat inside that output unseen - rows whose band collapsed to its FLOOR, all 21 storing a value LOWER than the authoritative issue price, none higher, average gap 8.63%, against a control where real-band issues price at the CAP in 46 of 46. Users saw a per-share price up to 12 rupees low on 21 listed IPO pages.
first_seen: Check added round-6 (T-308) for a real defect - a price-band collapse at close/listing. Premise over-generalised from the start; measured and rewritten 2026-09-11.
fix_prs: this PR - the check now flags three populations that are genuinely wrong (the stored price equals face_value; an authoritative listing_performance.issue_price disagrees with it; the band is degenerate while the book is still open) and stays silent on a closed issue priced at a plausible value. Real-data proof on staging: the SAME script goes from 239 violations to 28, and the 28 are named.
detection_check: scripts/tests/degenerate-band-check.test.mjs - drives the real predicate over all four outcomes; five mutations each proved applied and each turning it red, including restoring the OLD naive rule (fails 5 tests) and reading the COALESCE alias instead of the raw oracle. scripts/tests/audit-substance-plausibility.test.mjs statically proves the two new columns are SELECTed and goes red if either is dropped.
rule: Before flagging, ask which lifecycle state the rule is true in. A domain rule quoted from a regulation usually governs a PHASE (bidding open, before allotment, after listing), not the whole life of the row. A check that ignores the phase does not merely add noise - it trains readers to skip it, and the real cases then arrive invisible. And when an authoritative value for the field already exists in the caller's query, compare against it rather than asserting a shape.
